Thanks for adding the regression test and taking a stab at the fix! What do you think is proposed approach regarding the fix here? 

My initial look was that we are syncing all the pod status already [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L229-L230) however since in the issue the pod is rejected in pod admission, there are no calls to `kl.statusManager.TerminatePod(pod)` because the pod did not complete the usual `SyncTerminatingPod/SyncTerminatedPod`. Is that part of the problem here?

> Thanks for adding the regression test and taking a stab at the fix! What do you think is proposed approach regarding the fix here?

Sure, I'm happy with this as a fix to restore the 1.26 behavior. 

> My initial look was that we are syncing all the pod status already [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L229-L230) however since in the issue the pod is rejected in pod admission, there are no calls to kl.statusManager.TerminatePod(pod) because the pod did not complete the usual SyncTerminatingPod/SyncTerminatedPod. Is that part of the problem here?

I think in the long-term it might be better to go through `syncTerminatingPod`. However, (1.) it was not going through it on 1.26 in this scenario, so it is not a regression, (2) the benefit of going through `syncTerminatingPod` for non-amissible pods is limited as they never had containers running.

@bobbypage I would like to follow up with logs for this scenario. So indeed the pod does not go via `syncTerminatingPod`. Also: (1) it didn't before, (2) the pod wasn't admitted so has no resources claimed, (3) it goes via `syncTerminatedPod` which ensures all resources are cleaned up. 

I think it makes sense to bypass `syncTerminatingPod` for non-admissible pods, still it remains a question if this allows other pods to bypass `syncTerminatingPod`, but I don't see this possible.

I would also like to keep the fix small as we should cherry-pick for 1.27.

I had a chat with @bobbypage over the issue and PR. Here answering some of the questions from the meeting:

1. Isn’t podManager updated with `pod.Status.Phase=Failed`, so that on the next `syncBatch` we pass this awkward [check](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L901-L904), and delete can proceed?

Pod manager is indeed updated after the successful patch in `SyncLoop UPDATE` (see [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0330fd91f4f49505c34ca32558b2ddad2635eb68/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2603)). So in the next `syncBatch` indeed we have `status.status.Phase=pod.Status.Phase=Failed`. However, `podIsFinished` is `false` in this case. Thus, the method `needsUpdate` returns what `canBeDeleted` returns, which returns `false` [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0330fd91f4f49505c34ca32558b2ddad2635eb68/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L910).

2. Why in the proposed fixed version `syncTerminatedPod` is invoked?

Because after the successful `PATCH` (setting the phase as `Failed`) `canBeDeleted` returns `true` (after consulting pod workers [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e674ca2be2f66342497a618f26ba14fd0a83e7a9/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L908)). So we invoke the DELETE: 
 https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L872.
 
It triggers the `SyncLoop DELETE`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2425-L2427. 
 
This in turn triggers the pod_workers `UpdatePod`, which schedules a new `syncTerminatedPod` as `finished: false` [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0330fd91f4f49505c34ca32558b2ddad2635eb68/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L794) is set in this path since https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117019 . This also explains the difference with 1.26.

> Is there a succinct summary of the series of operations that prevents SyncTerminatedPod from running?

`SyncTerminatedPod` isn't called because this a new pod that is rejected at kubelet admission time. Since it was rejected at kubelet admission time, there is no pod worker driving it. 

> Or is this a net new pod that comes in that should be deleted? If it's the latter, we may still have to ensure the solution fixes the former (because that can also happen due to changing kubelet flags, devices, etc)

This is addressing the second case, this is a new pod that comes in that kubelet sees for the first time after it is started. When kubelet first sees the pod, the pod already has a deletion timestamp set. The pod is then rejected in kubelet admission time, but no-one ended up calling `TerminatePod` on it, so the status manager isn't allowed to delete the pod.

The first test, for the main scenario, fails consistently without the fix. 

The second, for the non-admissible runtime pod, passes as it was already covered by HandlePodCleanups, but it seems valuable to test this non-obvious modification of the main scenario.

Also lgtm on the changes, the change to use pod worker update with `SyncPodKill` is much cleaner then having to call into `TerminatePod` from within HandlePodCleanups.

The only thing I saw when testing out the changes [here](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/bobbypage/a6ff485744de4857837c5b6da8ebcadb/raw/6d1ed687c2c5e7411db799f95133c2b91e8800a9/gistfile0.txt) is there is a ~10s delay for the pod from the pod being rejected at kubelet to the pod being deleted on the apiserver. This is because the following flow happens:

(1) The pod is rejected by kubelet at admission and the local status manager is updated with terminal phase
(2) We wait 10s until the next [`syncBatch`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L158) completes in status_manager
(3) status manager sees that the local phase status is different then api status, it updates phase to failed
(4) HandlePodCleanups will run, pod is filtered as part of `filterTerminalPodsToDelete` and the SyncPodKill will be delivered to it.

IMO, the 10s latency is not big deal... it will reconcile eventually, but if we wanted it to update faster and reduce latency, I think if we also called `kl.podWorkers.UpdatePod(UpdatePodOptions` with `UpdateType: kubetypes.SyncPodKill` in `rejectPod` it would update the status ~instantly, without waiting for the 10sec sync batch (i.e. as https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118614/files). 

So maybe long term, we should do *both*, i.e. call `UpdatePod` in `HandlePodCleanups` and `rejectPod` for these types of pods that are rejected at admission and don't exist in pod worker. But I don't think should be blocking the PR (and can be handled as a followup) as the case here is not super common to hit in the first place, and the latency is not critical IMO.

### What happened?

We observed the following series of events:

1) Pod is created with some attributes that later result in the pod being rejected at kubelet admission time
2) The pod is scheduled to a node
3) The pod is gracefully deleted by a controller, i.e. a deletion timestamp is set on the pod
4) The pod is rejected at kubelet admission time
5) The pod never gets deleted and is stuck: despite having the deletion timestamp set. It seems that kubelet does not issue the final force delete for the pod.

This is problematic in many scenarios, but one specific case it was hit was when the pod is backed by a daemonset controller. This issue manifested in way where since the pod never got deleted in step 5 above, the daemonset controller did not create a new pod to run the on the node and thus node was was not running a replica of the daemonset controller pod.

This seems to a be regression in k8s 1.27, I was not able to repro this behavior in 1.26.

### What did you expect to happen?

It is expected at during the series of events above, after the pod is failed at kubelet admission time, since the pod has a deletion timestamp set, the kubelet should forcefully delete the pod. The pod should not hang in deletion forever.

I took a closer look at this and `HandlePodCleanups` is not handling this case. This is because the pod has been rejected at kubelet admission time, so a pod worker has not started for it. Additionally, the pod is not visible in the runtime, so it's not an orphan pod either. 

The main reason is because the pod has never started, so there is no pod worker driving it. The pod is returned from the desired state, pod manager (as part of `allPods` [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7cd51541cdc1fab211e22011e76052b997f5ce16/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1017). However, the pod is filtered out as part of `SyncKnownPods` because there was never a pod worker driving it, so there no [pod sync statuses](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7cd51541cdc1fab211e22011e76052b997f5ce16/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1539) for it. And since the pod is not part of `activePods` and it's not an orphan pod (since it doesn't exist in runtime because we haven't started it), we end up not do anything with it in `HandlePodCleanups`.

It's the "resync" action for the kubelet as controller, and so it's nominally responsible for forcing all other components (pod worker, status manager, runtime) to return to state. I don't think there is an issue from performance pov. 

First, the path is only invoked for terminal pods with the deletionTimestamp. The only scenario that produces such pods is described in the bug and is when the pod is non-admissible, and deleted during kubelet restart. So, it seems very unlikely to have many of such pods. 

Second, the TerminatePod is very fast as there is no killing of containers. I this the only reason it could take close to 2s is when the Delete request is throttled by the QPS or P&F at the API server side. However, since 1.27 the QPS for kubelet is 50, so we should be able to delete around 100 such pods in the 2s interval.

My concern here is that `TerminatePod` does call `updateStatusInternal` with `forceUpdate=true` (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2802bbce14ca32cddbd0d0567cd33fb435f445e6/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go).

Since `forceUpdate=true`, we will skip [this](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2802bbce14ca32cddbd0d0567cd33fb435f445e6/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L657-L660), and always create a new `versionedPodStatus` and trigger `syncBatch`. In `syncBatch` we send request to API-server which can take some time (throttling, P&F, etc). And since this is part of the `HandlePodCleanups` call, the time spent in `syncBatch` will block the main sync loop which is noted as [undesirable](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2802bbc/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L994-L999). 

Another alternative would be to refactor `TerminatePod` and have a way to mark the pod as terminated asynchronously so we don't trigger `forceUpdate=true` and have the pod termination be handled in the next `syncBatch`, that way it won't block the main `HandlePodCleanup` loop.
